subject: computing
title: Recursion: factorial(4) — the Call Stack Grows, Then Unwinds

segments.say: The calls descend: each call pauses and stacks a new frame. factorial(4) is called first, pauses, and calls factorial(3); that call pauses too and calls factorial(2). Point at the call stack on your student notes diagram before any value comes back.
questions: Which call runs first, and what does it do instead of finishing?
Where does factorial(4) wait while factorial(3) runs?

segments.say: Down to the base case: factorial(1) calls nothing. factorial(2) pauses and calls factorial(1), and factorial(1) answers at once with 1 - no new frame and no further call. Now try the base-case questions on your worksheet.
questions: Which call is the base case?
Why does the descent stop at factorial(1)?

segments.say: The stack unwinds: each frame resumes and multiplies. factorial(2) returns 2, factorial(3) returns 6, and the running products build 1, 2, 6, 24. Check the unwind order against your student notes before moving on.
questions: In what order do the frames resume?
What value does factorial(3) return, and how is it built?

segments.say: The outermost frame returns the answer. factorial(4) resumes last, multiplies 4 by 6, and returns 24; the stack is empty. Keep the descend, base case, unwind order as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
questions: What does factorial(4) return, and why is it last?
What are the four stages of the recursion, in order?
segments.watchFor: A recursive call replaces the caller, so factorial(4) is finished and gone once factorial(3) starts. Listen for students who say the first call ends when the next one starts, or who expect factorial(4) to finish first. Send them back to scene 1 and the growing call stack: The caller is not replaced: it is suspended on the call stack, still holding its place and its pending multiplication, and it resumes exactly where it stopped when the callee returns - which is why the stack unwinds in reverse order, multiplying 1, 2, 6, 24.
